comparable_reason: The paper-metric ratio is the well-behaved part. It is exactly width-invariant: zero-padding a 40-point circle from D = 2 to D = 8, 64 and 512 (an exact isometry) leaves zz_true_adjacent_mean at 1.000000 and n_bars at 1 in every case, and it is depth-normalized by beta_p(l1) rather than by a bar count. It is NOT depth-neutral on a structureless null: on iid Gaussian clouds redrawn per layer, zz_true_adjacent_mean falls 0.025641 (L=4) -> 0.012987 (8) -> 0.013445 (16) -> 0.004032 (32), Spearman -0.800 (n = 4, p = 0.20), because the bar population grows with the number of layers while genuine cross-layer survival does not. Separately, `zz_true_mean_bar_len` is measured in LAYERS and is mechanically depth-scaled (it is exactly L for a persistent loop), and the legacy weighted-geodesic band family (h1_total_layer_persistence, h1_max_band_length, h1_num_bands, h1_first/last_layer, betti1_fraction_layers) is an absolute-depth family with an unreachable persistence_frac = 0.3 threshold. On real models the ratio behaves: gpt2 0.591667 and distilgpt2 0.466667 at the shipped 40-sample config, with beta_1 > 0 at every layer (so the zero-Betti branch above is latent there and zz_true_adjacent_min/full_depth are genuinely 0.0 rather than NaN).
